frequency_question: What proportion of major bills complete the full sequence of Senate committee and floor processes within a 351-day timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes any primary legislative bill introduced, reported out of committee, and brought to a final passage vote in the U.S. Senate during a standard 12-month legislative sub-period. Excludes non-binding resolutions and purely ceremonial measures.

cases.name: Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act (H.R. 7888)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named major bipartisan/structural bills; thousands of minor bills omitted as non-comparable.
known_gaps: Excludes bills that stalled in committee due to lack of scheduling priority.
skeleton: Legislative cycles across recent Congresses where major standalone policy bills successfully navigated Senate floor time within a 351-day window.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 major observed major contested standalone structural bills tracked in recent session samples that reached final floor votes under time constraints.
validity_reason: Tied to the duration of the current 119th/120th Congress procedural rules framework.
